notes:
Status: stalled / at-risk. POC revealed a technical fit concern: their workload has frequent short-duration spikes (order dispatch and reranking during peak drop windows). During our simulated bursts we saw queuing and token-level latency growth — customer quote: 'We can't accept the 2-3x p95 during surge windows.'

Key ask: deterministic throughput during 1-2 minute spikes up to ~6k rps with sub-150ms p95 for reranking calls. They prefer a solution that guarantees pre-warmed capacity or instant burst capacity.

POC details: used hosted API with autoscale and prefix caching enabled. Observed slow warm-up of reserved instances; autoscaler lag ~30-60s into burst. Suggested fixes tried: larger initial worker pool, shorter cooldown, batching disabled for low-latency paths — improved, but still not within SLO for 90% of spike windows.

Decision drivers: 1) latency SLO for customer-critical flows; 2) budget — ops wants a predictable monthly commit vs unpredictable overage; 3) internal champion (lead infra) left in Jan, leaving procurement and SRE disaligned.

Recent communication: AE left a detailed proposal (Drive pricing + architecture) and two options: (A) Dedicated reserved pool with burst buffer + pre-warm SLA, (B) Private deployment on-prem with guaranteed nodes. Procurement paused due to annual headcount/budget freeze.

Competitive notes: CloudLane pitched fast pre-warm (edge presence) and a 'burst credits' pricing model. Customer commented 'CloudLane can demo our peak more easily today' in last procurement meeting.

Sales ask: try a short re-engagement 6-week plan offering a small pilot of Dedicated reserved burst pool (2 weeks) with defined success criteria (p95 < 150ms during synthetic 6k rps bursts) and an explicit burn-rate estimate. If procurement remains frozen, mark as closed-lost in 2026-06.
